record.paper_title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
record.original_question: Can PBH mass-spin correlations induced by accretion be used to determine the primordial nature of individual gravitational-wave events or of the event population, and how can uncertainties in the accretion model be reduced enough for population-level tests?

evidence.quote: The PBHs form in the early universe through the standard scenario of the collapse of large overdensities inherit a characteristic mass-spin correlations induced by accretion effects [7].
Using this criterion for determining the possible primordial nature of individual GW events would require reducing uncertainties on the accretion model and studied at the population level [59].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a population of black holes that may be of primordial origin, i.e., formed in the early universe by the gravitational collapse of large cosmological overdensities, rather than from stellar evolution. Suppose that, after formation, such primordial black holes (PBHs) accrete baryonic matter from the surrounding cosmological medium according to a spherical/disk accretion model that produces a deterministic correlation between the PBH mass M and dimensionless spin χ ∈ [0,1]: there exists a function χ_acc(M; θ) depending on accretion parameters θ (e.g., accretion onset redshift, efficiency, disk geometry) such that an isolated PBH of present-day mass M is predicted to have spin χ_acc(M; θ). Astrophysical (stellar-origin) black holes follow a distinct, generically different mass–spin distribution p_astro(M, χ).

(a) Formulate precise statistical criteria — for instance, a likelihood-ratio or Bayes-factor test on the joint mass–spin posterior of a single gravitational-wave merger event — under which the observation of an individual binary black hole event with measured (M, χ) suffices to identify it as primordial via the predicted accretion-induced mass–spin correlation, accounting for the measurement covariance of current/future GW detectors.

(b) At the population level, given N gravitational-wave events with posteriors on (M_i, χ_i), derive the dependence of the discrimination power (e.g., expected log Bayes factor between a primordial+astrophysical mixture model and a purely astrophysical model) on N and on the prior uncertainty in the accretion parameters θ. Determine quantitatively how tightly θ must be constrained, and how large N must be, so that the population-level test achieves a prescribed statistical significance (e.g., 5σ) for detecting (or excluding) a primordial subpopulation obeying the χ_acc(M; θ) relation.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of an open research roadmap on primordial black holes. Recent literature continues to develop accretion-driven mass–spin correlations as a discriminator between primordial and astrophysical black holes (e.g., De Luca, Franciolini, Pani, Riotto; Hütsi et al.), and population-level GW analyses with LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA data have placed only weak constraints, with the accretion model itself remaining a dominant systematic. No definitive resolution has been published; the status is open.

status_evidence.title: The evolution of primordial black holes and their final observable spins
status_evidence.snippet: We show that accretion onto PBHs in binaries induces characteristic correlations between their masses and spins.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the accretion-induced PBH mass–spin correlation that the question relies on.

status_evidence.title: Bayesian evidence for both astrophysical and primordial black holes in GWTC-3
status_evidence.snippet: Population analyses suggest a mixed origin remains viable but accretion-model systematics dominate.
status_evidence.claim: Population-level discrimination is limited by accretion-model uncertainties; question remains open.
